loss is strictly positive with a minimum of 0.67, so plain log(loss) is negative for some rows; the 2nd place winner used the shifted log(loss + 200) for that reason.
The metric is MAE, which targets the conditional median rather than the mean, so a mean-fitted gamma arm is systematically mis-aimed and must also be scored on MAE.
cont14 has a hard lower bound at 0.179722 and a range of 0.665122; check for a point mass at the bound before smoothing it.

The catalogue lists cont2 and cont3 under columns_to_exclude, but its own reason says they are a documented non-transform rather than an exclusion from the model, so both are kept as predictors.
No leakage, sentinel value or constant column is documented for this competition.

notes: 96 and 98 are survey-style 'other / don't know / refused' codes in the three past-due counters, not counts; they are declared as sentinels and mapped to missing before the adapter, and they occupy the same 269 rows in all three columns.

DebtRatio was computed by the sponsor as debt divided by coalesce(MonthlyIncome, 1), so on the 29,731 income-missing rows the cell holds the raw monthly debt amount rather than a ratio. One smooth over DebtRatio mixes two different units.

An integer-valued DebtRatio above 1 therefore implies a missing MonthlyIncome, and that cohort has a lower bad rate; the runner's MonthlyIncome missing indicator recovers part of this, the integer test is not built.

RevolvingUtilizationOfUnsecuredLines is defined as a fraction but reaches 50,708, and age runs to 109 with 489 rows above 90. Kaggle's own ruling was to use the data as it is; no capping or clipping is applied here.
There is no date column, so no temporal validation is possible; every winner used random cross-validation over the 150,000 rows.
Private AUC across the whole top 35 spans 0.001; judge any arm on repeated folds.

The label attaches to the card, not the transaction, and 68.2 per cent of private-test clients never appear in training, so no client identifier may enter as a level and a client-disjoint split cannot be certified from this table alone.

provenance.rules_accepted_by: the account holder on the competition page
provenance.publisher: IEEE Computational Intelligence Society with Vesta Corporation (competition host)
notes: This entry is train_transaction.csv alone. train_identity.csv is downloaded beside it but covers only a subset of TransactionIDs and joins left on TransactionID, so its id_01-id_38, DeviceType and DeviceInfo columns are absent here and their catalogue categorical declarations do not apply.
TransactionDT is a timedelta in seconds from a reference, not a timestamp; day = TransactionDT / 86400 and the series is believed to start on 1 December 2017.

The label attaches to the CARD: a reported chargeback marks that card's transactions fraudulent, so rows are not independent. Of 73,838 training clients with two or more transactions, 96.9 per cent are all-0, 2.9 per cent all-1 and 0.2 per cent mixed.

Missingness is structural and heavy (R_emaildomain 453,249 rows, dist2 552,913, M1-M9 over 269,000 each) and the V columns fall into blocks that share an identical NaN pattern; the protocol's missing-indicator companions and the 60-feature cap carry this, since the catalogue's 'redundant V columns inside each NaN block' exclusion names no columns.

Three further catalogue exclusion items are NOT applied because they are not column-drop claims: 'D1..D15 in raw form' asks for the Dxn = day - Dx transform, which no registry field can express and whose columns the catalogue itself carries in three known-good pairs; C3 is only excluded from the winners' within-uid aggregation, not from their feature set; and 'card1 as a raw level' is conditional on a model that cannot absorb unseen levels, whereas the shared adapter pools to the training levels with a cap of 32 and a fallback level.
The unnamed 'roughly 5 per cent of all columns, 19 features with single-feature AUC below 0.5' exclusion names no columns and so cannot be applied; the feature cap stands in for it.

Excluding TransactionDT as a predictor (the protocol's split-key-only rule) removes the left column of the three diagonal known-good pairs TransactionDT x D1, x D15 and x D10, including the only grade-A diagonal; the known-good arm will drop them for want of a present column.

notes: Official data description: 'All string type variables are categorical. There are no ordinal variables.' Every str column is therefore an unordered factor, and v38, v62, v72 and v129 are integer codes the catalogue also declares categorical.

v22 has 18,210 levels. It anchors four of the known-good pairs and needs shrunk or out-of-fold level statistics rather than raw per-level means; the adapter's 32-level cap plus a fallback level applies to every arm identically.
About 40 percent of the cells are missing, in blocks, across 119 of the 131 v-columns. The missingness is informative, so the runner's one-percent missing-indicator companions carry most of it.
-999 and -9999 appear in published pipelines as author-chosen fill values, not as pre-existing missing codes in the raw file; no sentinel is declared.
Every column is scaled with added anonymisation noise, and several float columns are latent integer counts on a lattice; knot placement from raw float quantiles will straddle lattice points.

The catalogue's third exclusion rule (drop one of each correlated pair at |r| > 0.9) is not applied: its specific column list was never recovered and would have to be re-derived from the training partition, which is a modelling step, not a registry one.

notes: target is the transformed ratio of loss to total insured value and is zero on 450,873 of 452,061 rows (99.74 per cent); 1,188 rows are non-zero. That is the compound Poisson-Gamma shape a Tweedie with 1 < p < 2 models directly.

var11 is the weight in the competition's var11-weighted normalised Gini and is declared here as weight_column. It also stays in the feature set: the 14th place competitor reports it worked much better as a covariate than as a weight, so both roles are live.

Level 'Z' in var1 to var9 is documented by the host as a missing value. It is NOT declared in sentinels: these are string categoricals where Z is a usable level, several teams found Z-ness itself predictive (var1_Z, var4_Z and var8_Z survive wallinm1's selectors), and the sentinel mechanism exists to keep spikes out of numeric splines.
var4 is hierarchical: 43 levels of the form <letter><digit>, the letter a higher level and the digit nested within it. Every top solution split the code.

The crime, geodemographic and weather blocks are joined-in region attributes with far fewer distinct combinations than rows (327, 2,588 and 24,531 respectively) and are heavily mutually redundant. Only the exclusions the catalogue enumerates by name are applied here; the remaining redundancy is left to the 60-feature cap.

var7 is mixed-dtype as shipped: the same eight codes appear both as strings and as integers. Measured here with the registry's own read_frame, an unconstrained read gives 17 'levels' ('1'..'8', 'Z', 1..8) where R and the pinned scan see 9, so each code would be split across two levels. source.read_csv pins dtype var7 to str, which restores the 9 documented levels and changes nothing else in the table. This is the one place this entry departs from 'read_csv for Allstate only'.
The train and test sets were split randomly, so there is no temporal validation axis.
Known-good pair firepe_dummy__var11 names dummy, which is excluded above, so the known-good arm will drop that pair.

datasets.feature_rank_source: The catalogue extension records no importance ranking for this competition; it reports the opposite ('feature engineering is genuinely low-yield', no top-4 solution dropped a predictor). The runner therefore ranks the 126 candidate predictors by training-only univariate Spearman correlation and keeps the top 60.

split.policy: random row split; no repeated units are documented

provenance.rules_accepted_by: the account holder on the competition page
notes: Response is an ordinal risk band 1..8. The protocol fits it as a numeric score with a Gaussian identity link, which is the 2nd- and 4th-place construction; the quadratic weighted kappa cut-point search that follows it in the competition is not run.

The host's own typing is followed for term selection: the 13 continuous columns (Product_Info_4, Ins_Age, Ht, Wt, BMI, Employment_Info_1/4/6, Insurance_History_5, Family_Hist_2/3/4/5), the 5 discrete Medical_History counts (1, 10, 15, 24, 32) and everything else on the nominal list as categorical, including Medical_Keyword_1..48.

Product_Info_2 is the only string column: a one-letter plus one-digit product code with 19 levels, declared categorical here; splitting it into letter and digit parts is an adapter decision, not a registry one.
All missingness sits in the 13 float64 columns and is informative; five of them are missing in over 40 percent of rows (Medical_History_10 at 58,824 of 59,381).
The table has no Insurance_History_6 despite the data page's 'Insurance_History_1-9' phrasing; do not build features from a range expression.
Quadratic weighted kappa at this sample size has about a 1 percent standard deviation, wider than the gap between 1st and 139th place.

datasets.title: Sberbank Russian Housing Market (train)
datasets.feature_rank_source: training_spearman: the catalogue extension records no importance-ranked single-feature list for this competition, so the protocol's fallback applies and the runner ranks the candidate predictors by a training-only univariate Spearman correlation with the response, keeping 60.

exclude_columns.id: Row identifier with no signal; no documented solution uses it as a feature.
exclude_columns.timestamp: Sale-date column reserved for the chronological split; the protocol derives year, month and day-of-week from it and those derived parts are the model's time terms.
exclude_columns.full_sq: It enters the linear predictor as the offset log(full_sq), which reproduces the 1st place's price-per-square-metre target exactly, so it must not also be a free predictor; the 1st place removed it as a direct feature because it contains many data errors.

split.policy: Chronological 60/20/20 cutoffs on timestamp with equal dates kept together. The competition rules permit look-ahead, so this is a modelling choice, not a competition constraint; the test period sits at a different price level, which every documented solution corrected multiplicatively.

provenance.rules_accepted_by: the account holder on the competition page
notes: The archive carries a __MACOSX/ directory entry and a __MACOSX/._train.csv resource fork beside train.csv; the reader addresses the CSV member by name and never extracts the archive, so those entries are inert.

The metric is RMSLE, so a Gaussian identity fit on log1p(price_doc) is that objective exactly; the offset log(full_sq) on the log scale reproduces the 1st place's price-per-square-metre target, since log(price_doc) = log(full_sq) + log(price per square metre).

full_sq contains many outright errors at both ends, and life_sq == full_sq is a data-entry sentinel for 'living area not recorded' rather than a measurement; that rule depends on a second column and cannot be expressed in the sentinels field, so it is left to the adapter and recorded here.

About 10 per cent of training rows are under-reported tax-avoidance prices, and the fake level is not a fixed rouble threshold ('In some areas 2 or 3 million were real prices, in other even 10 million were much lower than market'), so no row filter is declared; any pair result should be reported with and without such a filter.

build_year and max_floor carry sentinel and error values that the 1st place fixed by hand, and several distinct address labels are in reality one place (the 1st place identified individual buildings by the exact joint value of sub_area and kremlin_km).

sub_area (146 levels) and ecology are kept as categoricals: the 15th place dropped them only because XGBoost cannot take a string dtype, and the catalogue records them as 'must be encoded, not dropped'.

macro.csv is not registered locally, so the time trend has to come from price_doc itself; the host also issued corrected train and test files mid-competition, and this local train.csv is the original, so the winners' numbers will not reproduce exactly.
